thread:
emma: Hey team — escalating a customer issue. They report bursts of 429s to /v1/chat/completions even though their average QPS is ~2 and quota looks fine. Started after they upgraded to SDK 2.x. They say 10-20% of requests fail during short spikes and they see duplicate responses when retrying without idempotency keys.

raj: Do we have their request IDs or rate-limit headers? 429s should include Retry-After or X-RateLimit-* headers.

support-bot: auto-attach: recent support bundle for customer redacted-corp (req ids present, partial logs).

emma: Attached the bundle — they consistently get responses like:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 1
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1712345678
{
  "error": {"message": "rate limit exceeded", "type": "rate_limit"}
}
```

emma: But the weird part is X-RateLimit-Remaining toggles between 0 and 50 across subsequent requests even though their client concurrency is only 5. They run streaming chat calls with many short-lived connections.

raj: A few things to check: 1) Are they setting an idempotency key on non-idempotent chat streaming? Chat completions are not necessarily idempotent; retries without idempotency can cause duplicates. 2) Which SDK retry policy is enabled? 2.x SDK has an automatic retry wrapper — we changed the default backoff parameters in the last minor.

emma: Customer says SDK defaults are in use. They didn't set idempotency_key. They see retries happening client-side — sometimes a 429 triggers a retry, then get 200 but the message is duplicated. They're worried about cost and duplicate side effects.

sylvia: From support playbook: for chat endpoints, we recommend leaving automatic retries enabled only if you set an idempotency_key per user-turn, otherwise instruct customers to disable retries and implement client-side dedupe with a server-side token store.

raj: Quick repro steps for us to validate (please run in staging against their traffic pattern):
1) Simulate 5 concurrent streaming chat calls, each with 2-3 messages rapid-fire, for bursts of 30s.
2) Use SDK 2.1.0 vs 2.4.0 to compare behavior (we recently changed retry-on-429 to be softer).
3) Capture per-request headers, X-Request-ID, and whether client retried after 429 (and what delay used).

emma: I'm running a local sim now. Sample curl (non-streaming) to show headers we log: 

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-neo","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}], "stream":false}'
```

raj: Useful. Also capture the SDK debug trace (set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1) so we can see internal retry timings. Note: default SDK 2.x policy in our current release is: retries=3, base_delay=200ms, max_backoff=2200ms, jitter=full. It retries on 429 and >=500 but not on 4xx other than 429. If they had a different wrapper doing extra retries that could explain duplication.

sylvia: For support response: ask customer to do one of the following immediately to mitigate: 
- Option A (fast): Disable automatic SDK retries on chat endpoints and add dedupe server-side by storing a per-turn dedupe token.
- Option B (better): Send an idempotency_key header for each chat turn (if their UX tolerates dedupe) and keep retries on. This requires they generate stable keys per logical user-turn.
- Option C (enterprise): Move to Dedicated capacity — this is a common ask when unpredictable bursts hit shared quota.

emma: Customer also mentioned billing break alerts fired earlier in the day — could quota throttling be correlated? Their billing usage spiked for a different tenant the same hour.

raj: Quota exhaustion vs rate-limit: if their org-wide quota is exhausted you should see 429s with message referencing quota or a distinct error code. Rate-limit headers differ for per-key vs org-level. We should check their org's usage around the spikes.

support-bot: quick lookup: org-redacted shows a 3x usage spike at 2026-02-18T14:02:00Z — most of it from embeddings endpoint.

emma: So that could have consumed shared burst tokens and caused transient 429s on chat. Good catch.

raj: Action items for eng:
- Can runtime team confirm how shared burst tokens are allocated across endpoints and whether embedding-heavy spikes can starve chat pools? Tagging @eng-runtime.
- Also confirm that when Retry-After present we return consistent values for per-key and per-org limits.

deploy-bot: deploy: eng-runtime/patch-rate-limit-metrics @ 1772000489 — job kicked off.

raj: In the meantime, for support reply include a small code sample showing full-jitter exponential backoff they can plug in. Example (JS pseudo):

```
async function retryWithJitter(fn, attempts=3, base=200, max=2200) {
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try { return await fn(); }
    catch (e){
      if (!shouldRetry(e) || i===attempts-1) throw e;
      const exp = Math.min(max, base * Math.pow(2, i));
      const wait = Math.random() * exp; // full jitter
      await sleep(wait);
    }
  }
}
```

emma: Note: also recommend they check for hidden client concurrency like multiple browser tabs or serverless cold starts creating many short-lived sockets. Those cause bursts that bypass smooth rate-limiting assumptions.

sylvia: For ticket closure checklist: 1) customer confirms mitigation (idempotency or disable retries) 2) we confirm no org quota exhaustion test case for 24h 3) eng-runtime answers on token allocation and any platform fixes.

emma: I'll send the mitigation steps and ask for the SDK debug logs, request IDs, and a short recording of their traffic pattern. If eng-runtime confirms a bug, we'll coordinate a targeted patch and customer follow-up.

raj: If we find it's a shared-burst starvation issue, a potential quick fix is to prioritize chat traffic for interactive tiers and add soft reservation for small-burst traffic.

emma: Thanks. I'll update the ticket and ping here when we have logs. :thumbsup:
